title: Multiplicative and Additive Finite Free Convolutions for q-Polynomials
summary: We study $q$-analogs of finite free convolutions and their interaction with families of $q$-hypergeometric polynomials. First, we revisit the $q$-multiplicative finite free convolution, previously introduced in the literature, and show that it acts naturally on $q$-hypergeometric polynomials: the convolution of two such polynomials remains within the same class, with parameters obtained by concatenation. This observation provides a simple mechanism for constructing large families of $q$-hypergeometric polynomials whose zeros are real and whose logarithmic mesh is controlled. We illustrate it…
